stem: A plane electromagnetic wave of frequency \(25\,\text{MHz}\) travels in free space along the \(x\)-direction. At a particular point in space and time, \(\mathbf{E} = 6.3\,\hat{\mathbf{j}}\,\text{V/m}\). What is \(\mathbf{B}\) at this point?
solution:
Using \(B = E/c\) [Eq. (8.10)], the magnitude of \(\mathbf{B}\) is

\(B = \dfrac{E}{c} = \dfrac{6.3\,\text{V/m}}{3 \times 10^{8}\,\text{m/s}} = 2.1 \times 10^{-8}\,\text{T}\)

To find the direction, we note that \(\mathbf{E}\) is along the \(y\)-direction and the wave propagates along the \(x\)-axis. Therefore, \(\mathbf{B}\) should be in a direction perpendicular to both the \(x\)- and \(y\)-axes. Using vector algebra, \(\mathbf{E} \times \mathbf{B}\) should be along the \(x\)-direction. Since \((+\hat{\mathbf{j}}) \times (+\hat{\mathbf{k}}) = \hat{\mathbf{i}}\), \(\mathbf{B}\) is along the \(z\)-direction.

Thus, \(\mathbf{B} = 2.1 \times 10^{-8}\,\hat{\mathbf{k}}\,\text{T}\)
_note: The stated frequency of \(25\,\text{MHz}\) is not used anywhere in the book's printed solution; only the magnitude relation \(B = E/c\) and the propagation direction are needed. Transcribed faithfully.

stem:
The magnetic field in a plane electromagnetic wave is given by \(B_y = (2 \times 10^{-7})\,\text{T} \sin\left(0.5 \times 10^{3} x + 1.5 \times 10^{11} t\right)\).

(a) What is the wavelength and frequency of the wave?

(b) Write an expression for the electric field.
solution:
(a) Comparing the given equation with

\(B_y = B_0 \sin\left[2\pi\left(\dfrac{x}{\lambda} + \dfrac{t}{T}\right)\right]\)

We get, \(\lambda = \dfrac{2\pi}{0.5 \times 10^{3}}\,\text{m} = 1.26\,\text{cm}\),

and \(\dfrac{1}{T} = \nu = \dfrac{1.5 \times 10^{11}}{2\pi} = 23.9\,\text{GHz}\)

(b) \(E_0 = B_0 c = 2 \times 10^{-7}\,\text{T} \times 3 \times 10^{8}\,\text{m/s} = 6 \times 10^{1}\,\text{V/m}\)

The electric field component is perpendicular to the direction of propagation and the direction of the magnetic field. Therefore, the electric field component along the \(z\)-axis is obtained as

\(E_z = 60 \sin\left(0.5 \times 10^{3} x + 1.5 \times 10^{11} t\right)\,\text{V/m}\)
_note: PRINTED DEFECT in the book's own solution: the comparison equation is set as "B_y = B_o Sin[2p(x/lambda + t/T)]" — the page prints the letter p where the symbol pi belongs (a Symbol-font substitution) and capitalises Sin. It is transcribed here as \(2\pi\), which is unambiguously what the book means: its very next line computes \(\lambda = 2\pi/(0.5 \times 10^{3})\) using pi. No value or answer is affected.
